# Utility Bill Decoder (WTQ Build Track)

Reads a K-Electric, LESCO or IESCO electricity bill image and

1. **Level 1:** extracts the billing details into the required JSON schema, and
2. **Level 2:** answers customer questions about the bill in plain English, with every calculation done in code.

**Both result files, `level1.csv` and `level2.csv`, are generated by this code from the supplied templates. Nothing is edited by hand.**

**Runtime: Python 3.13** (3.11 or newer works). Optional React UI: Node.js 24 (22 or newer works).
Model access: a Google AI Studio API key (the free tier is enough).

## Submission layout

```
your-submission.zip
├── output/   level1.csv, level2.csv   <- produced by this code on the 10 official test bills
├── source/   this project: README.md, .env.example, requirements.txt, main.py, bill_decoder/, ...
└── demo/     demo.mp4                  <- screen recording of the solution
```

**All commands below are run from inside the `source/` folder.**

## 1. Setup

```bash
cd source
python -m venv .venv
```

Activate the environment:
- Windows PowerShell: `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`
- Windows cmd: `.venv\Scripts\activate.bat`
- macOS / Linux: `source .venv/bin/activate`

Install the dependencies (exact versions are pinned):

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Create your `.env` from the template, then open it and replace `your-api-key-here` with your Google AI Studio key:
- Windows: `copy .env.example .env`
- macOS / Linux: `cp .env.example .env`

`.env.example` already contains the real, non-secret settings (`MODEL_PROVIDER=google`, `MODEL_NAME=gemini-3.5-flash-lite`,
`VERIFIER_MODEL_NAME=gemini-3.1-flash-lite`); only `API_KEY` needs your value. The real `.env` is never part of the submission.

## 2. Generate the CSV files

Point the program at the official **test folder**, which contains `bills/` (the images) and `csv/` (the `level1.csv` and `level2.csv` templates):

```
<TEST_FOLDER>/
├── bills/   KESC_0002.png, IESCO_0002.jpg, ...
└── csv/     level1.csv, level2.csv
```

Run (replace `<TEST_FOLDER>` with the real path):

```bash
python main.py --bills <TEST_FOLDER>/bills --csv <TEST_FOLDER>/csv --out results
```

For example, on Windows: `python main.py --bills C:\data\test\bills --csv C:\data\test\csv --out results`
(use `.venv\Scripts\python main.py ...` if you did not activate the environment).

This reads every bill, fills in the templates and writes **`results/level1.csv`** (one row per bill, one-line JSON) and
**`results/level2.csv`** (one row per bill and question). `bill_id`, `question_id`, `question` and the row order are copied
unchanged from the templates. It writes to `results/` so it never overwrites the submitted `output/` folder.

Notes:
- The free Gemini tier allows 15 requests per minute, so the program paces itself; a full run takes roughly 10 minutes for 10 bills.
- Finished work is cached per bill in `.cache/`. If a run is interrupted, run the same command again and only unfinished bills are redone. `--no-cache` forces a fresh run.
- The submitted `output/` files were produced by exactly this command on the official test bills. Because the models are probabilistic, a fresh re-run can differ slightly in wording or in a few borderline values.

Check the generated files (row counts, columns, JSON validity, no empty cells):

```bash
python dev/check_submission.py <TEST_FOLDER>/csv results
```

It prints `PASS` when the files are valid.

## 3. Optional: user interfaces and tests

These are for exploring and verifying results; they are **not** needed to produce the CSVs.

```bash
pip install -r requirements-ui.txt      # Streamlit, FastAPI, pytest, ...
```

| What | Command (from `source/`) | URL |
|---|---|---|
| Streamlit app (decode, verify, ask) | `streamlit run app.py` | http://localhost:8501 |
| HTTP API (for the React UI) | `uvicorn api:app --port 8000` | http://localhost:8000/docs |
| React UI (needs the API running) | `cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev` | http://localhost:8080 |

Start the API first, then the React UI in a second terminal. `frontend/` is a React 19 + TypeScript (TSX) + Tailwind app that
talks to the HTTP API; `VITE_API_URL` in `frontend/.env.local` (template: `frontend/.env.example`) points to it
(default `http://localhost:8000`). It shows the extracted bill, consistency checks, a second-model opinion, comparison with
expected values, and a Q&A chat with the calculation steps. Upload any bill image to use it (the "sample bill" buttons only
appear if a `data/train/train/bills` folder exists next to `source/`).

Tests and scoring helpers:

```bash
pytest -q tests                             # unit tests (parsing, calculator, validation, voting, CSV writing)
python dev/evaluate.py results/level1.csv   # score Level 1 against answer keys in tests/gold/ (KESC_0008)
cd frontend && npm test                     # front-end tests
```

## 4. How it works

```
image -> preprocess (EXIF fix, size cap)
      -> Level 1: Gemini vision read (provider-specific hints, schema + rules prompt)
                  -> deterministic normalisation (numbers, CR -> negative, dates, enums, zero lines)
                  -> arithmetic validation (charges/taxes sums, readings vs units, totals, dates)
                  -> if a check fails: four more independent readings (alternating the two allowed models) are taken
                     and each field is decided by majority vote (printed values are never "corrected" by code;
                     the vote only picks among values the model actually read)
      -> Level 2: fact-sheet transcription (usage history, line items, late-payment amounts, notes)
                  -> planner lists the calculations each question needs
                  -> a safe calculator in Python evaluates them (sums, averages, counts, projections)
                  -> answer writer uses the exact results, states interpretations, labels estimates,
                     and says so when the bill does not show something
```

Design choices: the model is used where it adds the most value (reading messy, tilted, bilingual images and
explaining in plain language); code is used where it is more reliable (number parsing, validation, arithmetic, CSV writing).
Every API call is rate-paced for the free tier, retried with backoff, and can fall back to the other allowed model.
A failure on one bill never stops the run; that bill gets a valid fallback row instead.

Project layout: `bill_decoder/` (library: `llm`, `extract`, `qa`, `validate`, `schema`, `csv_io`, `pipeline`, ...),
`main.py` (CLI), `app.py` (Streamlit), `api.py` (HTTP API), `frontend/` (React UI), `dev/` (evaluation, checker, packager), `tests/`.

## 5. Configuration (`.env`)

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `MODEL_PROVIDER` | `google` |
| `MODEL_NAME` | primary model: `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` |
| `VERIFIER_MODEL_NAME` | cross-check / fallback model: `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` |
| `API_KEY` | Google AI Studio key (placeholder in `.env.example`; never commit the real one) |
| `MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `MAX_RETRIES`, `CACHE_DIR` | optional tuning (defaults shown in `.env.example`) |

## AI usage

- **Models called by the solution (only these two):** Google `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` (primary) and
  Google `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` (second readings / fallback), through the Google AI Studio API using the `google-genai` SDK.
- **Other APIs / services / OCR / invoice-extraction tools:** none.
- **AI tools used to write the code:** Claude Code (Anthropic) for the Python solution, tests and tooling;
  Lovable to generate the React front end in `frontend/`.
